note.text: Logic helps us judge reasons, communicate clearly and revise beliefs when evidence changes. It does not make every belief correct or remove the need for factual investigation. Relevant evidence addresses the claim at issue. Consistent claims can hold together without contradiction in the same circumstances. A fallacy is a mistake in reasoning. The value of a conclusion should be assessed through the reasons, rather than through the speaker's status or the popularity of the claim.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Logic helps us judge reasons, communicate clearly and revise beliefs when evidence changes. It does not make every belief correct or remove the need for factual investigation. Relevant evidence addresses the claim at issue. Consistent claims can hold together without contradiction in the same circumstances. A fallacy is a mistake in reasoning. The value of a conclusion should be assessed through the reasons, rather than through the speaker's status or the popularity of the claim.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A Douala club must choose whether to repair its reading room. A report on the leaking roof is relevant. The colour of the chairperson's shirt is not. The club can ask for evidence without attacking the speaker. If a measurement was wrong, admitting and correcting it improves the discussion rather than showing defeat.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Ask what would count as evidence and whether the offered reason concerns that issue. Check whether claims conflict under the same conditions. Challenge an inference politely; do not confuse criticism of a reason with an insult to its author. A good process can still begin with incomplete information, so remain open to correction.

key_words.meaning: a reason's bearing on the claim under discussion
claims being able to hold together without contradiction in the same respect
information used to support or test a factual claim
a mistake in the reasoning offered

examples: A proposal to repair a roof cites water entering through holes.
The club says its door is open this afternoon and not locked this afternoon.
A learner checks a rain gauge before reporting rainfall.

mistake.why: The evidence must bear on the particular conclusion; interest alone is insufficient.
